 Daily Tax Report State Print Email Share To: Facebook LinkedIn Microsoft Demands $212 Million New Jersey Corporate Tax Refund
 Oct. 30, 2026, 1:31 AM UTC Amy Lee Rosen Microsoft Corp. sued the Director of New Jersey’s Division of Taxation after the denial of its corporate business tax refund claim, and is seeking $212.82 million over foreign income the technology company says had little connection to the state.
 Microsoft filed the suit in the Tax Court of New Jersey after the division rejected the company’s argument that the state’s method of taxing a category of foreign income — known as Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income, or GILTI — inflated the share of that income attributed to New Jersey.
